syndicRelances.emptyEligible: ✓ No reminders to send. All eligible unpaid items already received their tier.
syndicRelances.emptyHistory: No reminders sent for this condominium.

syndicRapprochement.adviceBody: export the CSV statement from your LU web banking (BCEE: Menu » Statements » CSV export · BIL: Accounts » History » CSV). Matches scored ≥ 60 are reliable (exact reference + amount). Scores 30–59 need manual validation.

syndicAssemblyDetail.confirmDeleteRes: Delete this resolution and all its votes?
syndicAssemblyDetail.emptySelectRes: Select a resolution from the agenda.
syndicAssemblyDetail.votesTitle: Votes per unit ({ok} expressed out of {total})
syndicAssemblyDetail.infoBody: co-owners can vote from their personal area (portal link) on resolutions of a meeting in «convened» or «in progress» state. Votes are weighted by shares and the result is recalculated automatically based on the majority type (simple / absolute / double / unanimity).

proaFicheBien.pageSubtitle: Commercial brochure based on your information. Initial numbers are examples to replace; no independent valuation is calculated here.
proaFicheBien.fieldEstimatedHint: The range applies your percentage to your central value. It is neither a confidence interval nor a Tevaxia appraisal.
proaFicheBien.usageBody: Commercial brochure based on your information. Initial numbers are examples to replace; no independent valuation is calculated here.

proaPerformance.pageSubtitle: Agents ranked by commissions earned in {year}, with conversion / sales cycle / pipeline metrics. Visible to organisation admins.
proaPerformance.emptyAgents: No agent with mandates visible in your scope.
proaPerformance.infoTitle: USALI metrics (revenue management adapted to real estate):
proaPerformance.infoBody: conversion = closed sales / signed mandates · sales cycle = time from signing to authentic deed. A cycle < 90 days is healthy in the LU market. Conversion > 70% indicates good lead quality. Pipeline × average probability = T+3 month commission projection.

proaCommissions.pageSubtitle: Annual summary of commissions earned and pipeline. Useful for personal tax filing (LU income tax, self-employed category).
proaCommissions.pipelineHint: Estimated commission if all active mandates closed at asking price.
proaCommissions.fiscalityBody: real estate agent commissions are taxable as self-employed income (art. 91 LIR), with professional expenses deductible from turnover. Co-mandates are split at notarial deed signing, this table allocates your share automatically.

proaCrmTemplates.pageSubtitle: 10 ready-made email templates for the most common LU real estate situations. Variables auto-substituted. Opens your mail client directly with a pre-filled mailto:.
proaCrmTemplates.emptyPanel: Select a template on the left to customise and send.
proaCrmTemplates.usageBody: adjust the variables to your context (client first name, property address, price…) then click «Open in my mail client». Mailto will open Gmail, Outlook or Apple Mail depending on your OS config with subject + body pre-filled. Templates are versioned in the code (no database), request an addition / change through your usual channels.

proaSignatures.pageDesc: Online signature workflow compliant with EU regulation 910/2014 (eIDAS). "Simple electronic signature" level — valid for commercial mandates. For notarial deeds, qualified LuxTrust signature is required (roadmap Q5).

proaSignatures.eidasNotice: eIDAS proof retained: upon signing, the platform records the IP address, browser, timezone and server timestamp, all made immutable via a DB trigger. The document is identified by its SHA-256 hash — any subsequent modification invalidates the signature and triggers an alert.

Between the undersigned:
The PRINCIPAL: {client}
represented by themselves.

acting through a qualified and registered real-estate agent
in accordance with the law of 28 December 1988 regulating real-estate
professions.

Article 1 — PURPOSE OF THE MANDATE
The principal grants the agent a {mandateType} mandate to sell
the property located at:
{address}
{commune}
Type: {propertyType}

The net seller price is set at {price}.

The agent's commission is set at {commissionPct}% of the sale price

{exclusiveClause}

coproAssistant.title: Co-owner assistant

pmsForecast.pageDesc: OTB (On The Books) projection plus a conservative pickup extrapolated from the last 30 days. Automatic alert when forecast occupancy is below threshold at D-14, D-7 or D-2.
pmsForecast.alertNoneOk: ✓ No alerts. Projected occupancy within norm across the full horizon.
pmsForecast.alertCriticalJ2: Low occupancy at D-2. Price drop or last-minute marketing recommended.
pmsForecast.alertWarningJ7: Projected occupancy low at D-7. Revise rates or open a discount rate plan.
pmsForecast.alertWarningJ14: Occupancy < 50% at D-14. Reactivate OTA channels.
pmsForecast.eventsTip: Events with high or extreme impact typically justify a +20% to +40% rate uplift. Enable stop-sell or 2-night MinLOS to maximise RevPAR.
pmsForecast.methodology: Methodology: {methodology}. Pickup is weighted at 40% for prudence (conservative Revenue Management approach). For a more aggressive projection in known high-demand periods (events, seasonality), adjust manually via rate plans and restrictions. At D-14, D-7 and D-2, use the alerts to trigger actions: price drop, MinLOS, discount rate plan, OTA campaign.
pmsForecast.methodologyText: OTB + conservative 40% pickup × pickup_rate of last 30 days

pmsHeatmap.pageDesc: 365-day calendar view coloured by occupancy rate. Spot low seasons, weekend patterns and impactful events at a glance.
pmsHeatmap.emptyYear: No night audit recorded for {year}. Audits are generated automatically every night (auto-close roadmap) or manually from the <link>reservations</link> page.
pmsHeatmap.methodology: How to read: hover a day to see occupancy + revenue details. Darker colour means more rooms sold. Useful to identify low-season gaps and adjust rates or marketing campaigns in advance.

pmsPickup.pageDesc: Reservations booked in the recent window, broken down by future stay month and source. Critical revenue-management KPI for adjusting rates, restrictions (MinLOS, CTA) and distribution channels.
pmsPickup.emptyWindow: No reservations created in this window. Adjust the horizon or check your distribution channels.
pmsPickup.methodology: Revenue Management: use this report to detect abnormal pickup (positive or negative) and adjust rates or restrictions accordingly. Low pickup on a near month justifies a price drop or opening discount rate plans. Excessive pickup allows raising rates and closing 1-night MinLOS.

pmsUsali.pageDesc: Uniform System of Accounts for the Lodging Industry v11. Global AHLA / HOTREC standard. Occupancy / ADR / RevPAR / TRevPAR KPIs plus revenue breakdown by department and YoY comparison.
pmsUsali.methodology: USALI v11: global hospitality reporting standard (AHLA and HOTREC). Adopted by the Big 4 (PwC, Deloitte, EY, KPMG) for hotel benchmarking. The official KPIs are ADR, RevPAR and TRevPAR, with RevPAR being the synthetic performance measure (ADR × occupancy).

propcalcDevelopers.frenchFeesInputs: France: price includes VAT when applicable. With isNew=true, provide frenchVatOnFullPrice (a new sale subject to VAT on the full price, excluding margin VAT). If true, frenchVatRate is required: 0.055, 0.1 or 0.2. If false, ordinary transfer taxes are modeled. loanGuaranteeCost is a quoted guarantee cost, accepted only with a loan; if absent, it remains unpriced. acquisitionCoverage lists excluded costs: totalFees is a subtotal, not a complete notarial statement.
propcalcDevelopers.frenchRentalInputs: French rental taxation (/yield): taxYear is 2025 or 2026 (default 2026). The default is reel_foncier, a simplified unfurnished actual-expense scenario. Micro regimes require frenchMicroEligible=true to confirm eligibility and aggregate household/activity receipts, including prior-year micro-BIC conditions. Furnished rental requires frenchNonProfessional=true. micro_bic means long-term rental, micro_bic_tourism classified tourism, and micro_bic_tourism_unclassified unclassified tourism. annualTaxReceipts supplies aggregate taxable receipts, including taxable tenant charges; otherwise modeled rent after vacancy is used. frenchSocialRegime=solidarity_only requires qualifying social-insurance affiliation; standard is the default. The marginal-rate calculation is not a household tax assessment. Activity contributions, loss carryovers and special regimes are excluded.
propcalcDevelopers.ukFeesInputs: UK (/fees, country=uk): region accepts ENG, NIR, SCT or WLS; omitted means an explicit ENG assumption. ukAdditionalProperty confirms higher-rate liability independently of isPrimary; ukNonResident qualifies the non-resident SDLT surcharge in England/Northern Ireland. Both default to false. First-buyer relief requires isFirstTime and isPrimary, with every buyer eligible; Wales has no specific first-buyer relief. Only ordinary residential purchases by individuals are modeled, excluding transitional rules, companies, linked transactions and new lease rents. acquisitionCoverage describes the subtotal and excluded fees. /cashflow assumes an additional purchase in England without the non-resident surcharge.
propcalcDevelopers.italianRentalInputs: Italy (/yield): only 21% cedolare_secca for an ordinary residential free-market lease is calculated. italianCedolareEligible=true confirms an eligible individual landlord outside business/professional activity and a valid election for this regime. italianAnnualContractRent is required: gross contractual rent for the ownership share and rental period, without expense deductions. Modeled vacancy reduces economic receipts but does not automatically change this tax base. Negative rental cash income does not cancel the tax. IRPEF, short lets, reduced-rate contracts, unpaid rent and special cadastral cases require a separate assessment.
propcalcDevelopers.portugueseRentalInputs: Portugal (/yield): portugueseCategoryFConfirmed=true confirms ordinary category F rental and tax-eligible paid expenses. portugueseRentalUse is housing or other. portugueseAnnualTaxReceipts and portugueseDeductibleExpenses are required, including zero: modeled economic expenses are not automatically tax deductions. Interest, depreciation, furniture, appliances, decor and AIMI are excluded from deductions. taxYear is 2025 or 2026. Autonomous rates: housing 25%, other rental 28%, for residents and non-residents. For housing in 2026, portugueseModerateRentEligible must explicitly be true or false: true confirms all conditions and monthly-rent limits under EBF article 45-C / DL 97/2026 article 2 to apply 10%. Do not infer eligibility from annual rent after vacancy. More favourable long-duration rates, exemptions and special regimes need a separate assessment. progressive_resident uses the supplied marginal rate, without automatic comparison or household tax assessment.

access.title: How to access your portal
access.intro: No account creation. Your syndic sends you a secure personal magic link.

steps.title: Request from syndic
steps.desc: Contact your professional or volunteer syndic and request your tevaxia co-owner access link.

steps.title: Receive by email
steps.desc: You receive an email with your personal link. Keep it — valid as long as not revoked.

steps.title: Direct access
steps.desc: Click the link: you reach your file without a password. No app to install.

access.note: Haven't received a link? Your syndic may not use tevaxia yet. Invite them to discover our syndic solution.

items.q: Is the link secure?
items.a: The token is random (256 bits), unique and opaque. It strictly identifies your lot and your data. You can ask your syndic to revoke it at any time.

items.q: Can I vote at the AGM from the portal?
items.a: Yes, on resolutions open for electronic voting. Luxembourg law of 16 May 1975 (amended 6 June 2023) allows remote voting unless the co-ownership rules forbid it.

items.q: What if I'm also a tenant elsewhere?
items.a: You can have multiple separate accesses (one per co-ownership lot + one per rental lease). Each token is independent.

items.q: Is my data stored in Europe?
items.a: Yes. tevaxia hosts all data in the European Union (Supabase EU + Vercel EU). GDPR compliant.

items.q: How much does this access cost me?
items.a: Co-owner access is free. Your syndic subscribes to tevaxia to manage the co-ownership.

steps.desc: You are elected to the syndic council by the general assembly (Article 15-1, Law 1975).

steps.title: Link sent by syndic
steps.desc: The syndic sends your personal syndic council access link by email.

steps.title: Permanent access
steps.desc: Connect any time from any device. No password required.

access.note: The syndic council mandate is time-limited (usually 1 to 3 years). Your access is revoked at the end of the mandate.

items.q: What are my legal duties?
items.a: The syndic council assists and oversees the syndic. It must be consulted for any contract above a threshold set by the AGM (Article 15-1, Law of 16 May 1975 as amended).

items.q: Can I see accounting documents?
items.a: Yes, the syndic council can access supporting documents at any time. tevaxia gives access to invoices scanned by the syndic.

items.q: What if I detect an anomaly?
items.a: Report it to the syndic via tevaxia messaging (traceability kept). In case of dispute, the council can call an extraordinary AGM.

items.q: How many council members?
items.a: Luxembourg law sets no fixed number. Practice is 3 to 5 members for a medium-sized co-ownership.

steps.title: View shared records
steps.desc: Open the link without creating an account. Access depends on its expiry date and any revocation.

access.note: Keep the link confidential: anyone holding it can access the shared information. Contact your landlord if you do not have a link.

items.q: Can I download a signed rent receipt?
items.a: This screen shows rent entries and an issue date when recorded. Ask your landlord for a signed receipt document.

items.q: Is the balance complete?
items.a: It covers displayed entries only. A partial payment without a known amount makes the balance unknown; confirm the complete position with your landlord.

items.q: Are the deposit and inspection reports available?
items.a: The current portal does not track deposit movements or provide inspection reports and detailed supporting documents for charges. Ask your landlord for them.

items.q: How long is the link valid?
items.a: The link has an expiry date and can be revoked. Its duration does not automatically match the lease; an additional 12 months of access after departure is not guaranteed.

items.q: What if information is incorrect?
items.a: Contact your landlord with the period and amount concerned. This read-only space cannot be used to pay rent or edit the records.

plusValuesAudit.title: Property capital gain — Luxembourg 2025–2026
plusValuesAudit.scope: Simulation of a private property sale by a resident in tax class 1 or 2. Enter your ownership share only, or the shares of the jointly assessed household. Use the deed dates and effective transfer of ownership.
plusValuesAudit.transmission: Use the price, eligible costs and date of the previous holder’s last purchase for consideration. The declared inheritance or gift value does not replace that price.
plusValuesAudit.dateAcquisition: Date of last purchase for consideration
plusValuesAudit.justificatifs: Actual documented costs without double deductions. This screen accepts one group of improvements; combine only expenses from the same year. Purchase costs and improvements are revalued separately, except for speculative gains.
plusValuesAudit.transitoire: Agreement registered with AED by 30 June 2025
plusValuesAudit.transitoireHint: For a sale from 1 July to 30 September 2025, this condition preserves the two-year holding threshold and quarter global rate.
plusValuesAudit.revenuHint: After applicable deductions and allowances, excluding this gain. Zero is valid. Other extraordinary income and foreign income exempt with progression are outside this mode.
plusValuesAudit.abattements: €50,000 / €100,000 allowances used in the previous ten years
plusValuesAudit.abatSuccessionHint: Direct-line inheritance of the parents’ last principal home: personal one-time limit of €75,000. Joint assessment permits €75,000 per spouse on their own eligible inherited share; €150,000 only if both personally qualify.
plusValuesAudit.rp: I confirm that the principal-home exemption conditions are met
plusValuesAudit.rpHint: Calling a property your principal home is insufficient. Check actual occupation, departure date and assimilation conditions in the ACD guide.
plusValuesAudit.dependance: Resident covered by Luxembourg long-term care insurance
plusValuesAudit.autresDependance: Other positive net asset-income bases for long-term care contribution
plusValuesAudit.erreur: Check amounts, exact dates and improvement year. Sale in 2025–2026, purchase from 1941. Inheritance allowances must match the acquisition method and personal limit.
plusValuesAudit.exonere: Principal home — exemption confirmed by your answers
plusValuesAudit.regime: Applicable holding threshold: {annees} years. Global-rate fraction for a disposal gain: {fraction}. Speculative gains follow the ordinary tariff.
plusValuesAudit.coefficient: ACD coefficient for the sale year
plusValuesAudit.fraisReevalues: Costs and improvements after applicable revaluation
plusValuesAudit.produit: Sale proceeds after costs and tax provision
plusValuesAudit.provision: For speculative gains, the employment fund is calculated by tariff difference. For disposal gains it is a provision of 7% of income tax, or a 7–9% range above €150,000 (class 1) / €300,000 (class 2). Allocation to extraordinary income must be settled with the annual tax assessment; this provision is not a final tax assessment.
plusValuesAudit.produitHint: Sale proceeds are not profit: the purchase price is not deducted here. Outstanding debt, unentered mortgage-release fees and other commitments remain payable.
plusValuesAudit.limitations: One transaction and no other gains or losses to offset. Annual speculative gains below €500 are exempt. Reinvestment relief, share sales, business assets, non-residents, class 1a, extraordinary deductions under article 131(3) and minimum bases for old acquisitions require separate analysis. The sale must still be declared even if exempt.

estimationAudit.title: Estimation data and limitations
estimationAudit.limits: Freehold apartments only. Adjustments are internal assumptions, without validation against an independent sales sample. The ±18% range (±25% for asking prices only) is a convention, with no guaranteed accuracy or probability.
estimationAudit.missing: No estimate is available for these inputs. Check the area and published data for the sale type. Suppressed official prices are not invented.
estimationAudit.period: Period: 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 (rolling 12 months). Recorded prices include annexes; the estimator uses adjusted prices excluding annexes where available. Asking prices are not completed sales.
estimationAudit.assumptions: These percentages are working assumptions, not official Observatory coefficients. No MAPE, R², significance or accuracy on real sales has been demonstrated.
estimationAudit.formula: Price = municipal mean × (1 + sum of adjustments / 100) × floor area. No individual neighborhood prices. For VEFA, no automatic premium for new condition or energy rating: the VEFA source already reflects that segment.
estimationAudit.vefa: Published VEFA prices include 3% VAT, subject to the €50,000 tax benefit limit. Adapt this basis if your purchase is ineligible. Parking is a +4% assumption only on the basis excluding annexes; cellars and other annexes are not valued separately.
estimationAudit.suppression: Suppressed prices remain unavailable: fewer than 10 recorded sales or 30 advertisements in these files. Synthetic examples are not comparable sales and do not measure model reliability.
estimationAudit.disclaimer: Indicative estimate using internal assumptions. Read the methodology before use.

fiscalGuideAudit.updated: Calculation guides — rules checked on 8 September 2026
fiscalGuideAudit.pvRegime: In 2026, private sales held for no more than five years are speculative; longer holdings may qualify for half the overall tax rate. In 2025, the two-year threshold and quarter overall rate apply through 30 June, and from 1 July to 30 September if the preliminary agreement was registered with AED by 30 June. Exact dates matter.
fiscalGuideAudit.pvAbat: For long-term sales, the remaining ten-year allowance of €50,000 (€100,000 for joint assessment) follows other eligible deductions and the eligible inheritance allowance. It does not apply to speculative gains. Income tax depends on ordinary income and tax class; a universal flat rate would be misleading.
fiscalGuideAudit.rentRule: The annual rent cap excluding charges is 5% of revalued invested capital after net depreciation. It is neither 5% of current market value nor a guaranteed yield. Recoverable charges are separate.
fiscalGuideAudit.rentCoef: Revaluation uses the annual Article 102 LIR table published by ACD. Purchase price, eligible fees and each improvement use their respective years; future work is excluded. Furniture is not part of this property capital.
fiscalGuideAudit.rentFurniture: Under the current furnished tenancy regime, the monthly supplement is capped at 1.5% of eligible invoices for furniture less than ten years old. There is no automatic 20% uplift on property rent.
fiscalGuideAudit.rentExample: Verifiable example: built in 1970, bought in 2000 for €380,000 plus €28,000 fees; land €81,600; improvements €15,000 in 2000; lease in 2020. With coefficient 1.4 and no deductible maintenance: revalued capital €592,200, depreciation €95,592, net capital €496,608, monthly cap €2,069.20.
fiscalGuideAudit.rentScope: Land followed by construction, spending over several years and special regimes require appropriate allocation. Keep deeds, invoices and evidence; a municipal average does not replace invested capital.

acquisitionAudit.prixHT: Project price excluding VAT (land + construction net of VAT)
acquisitionAudit.invalid: Check amounts, ownership shares and personal credits.
acquisitionAudit.creditHint: The credit balance is personal: check AED/MyGuichet. The suggested €40,000 assumes no previous use. One buyer’s balance cannot be transferred to another. A minimum €100 remains payable for the deed.
acquisitionAudit.nonResident: EEA residents may request the credit when committing to move into the property. Residents outside the EEA must advance the duties until they provide a Luxembourg residence certificate: the result then shows the cost after any refund.
acquisitionAudit.mortgageHint: Loan principal. Add below any ancillary amounts included in the secured registration base.
acquisitionAudit.mortgageScope: Ordinary non-exempt mortgage loan: 0.24% of principal, 0.05% of the secured amount, tariff 5 and VAT. Exemptions, mortgage discharge, copies and bank fees are not calculated.
acquisitionAudit.notaryScope: Private sale: tariff 7 of the notarial regulation, minimum €99.16 excluding VAT, plus 17% VAT. Copies, disbursements, travel and exceptional work must be added from the notary’s statement.
acquisitionAudit.vefaScope: Off-plan: enter a price excluding VAT. This mode assumes no construction completed at the deed, all construction eligible and the full €50,000 VAT benefit still available for personal occupation. Started projects or previously used benefits need an individual statement.
acquisitionAudit.scope: Partial fee estimate under documented rules. The credit uses the €40,000 ceiling confirmed by the law of 3 July 2025. The increase to €45,000 announced in July 2026 is not included without confirmation that it has entered into force.

aidesAudit.title: Housing assistance: 2026 estimate
aidesAudit.intro: Calculate grants for your situation and distinguish tax relief from assistance that still needs assessment. Prefilled figures are examples; confirm conditions and remaining allowances before relying on an amount.
aidesAudit.date: Rules and sources checked on 8 September 2026. Ordinary scheme for 2026 deeds and new applications.
aidesAudit.worksNote: A total budget cannot determine Klimabonus: technical measures, dates and quotes are required.
aidesAudit.incomeNote: Statutory income after contributions and withheld tax, including foreign income and maintenance, excluding dependent children’s income. Purchase grant: 2024/2025 average; interest: 2025. Cases without two income years require individual review.
aidesAudit.accessionConfirm: I confirm ordinary eligibility: adult beneficiaries with residence rights, full ownership, mortgage, no more than one third of another home, no affordable/cost-price sale, required occupancy and timely application. Income and remaining allowances are checked.
aidesAudit.savingsHint: Actual amounts separated by ; (example: 2000; 3500; 5000). One to ten years. Leave blank if unknown.
aidesAudit.savingsConfirm: Savings held at the same institution for at least one year, documented increases and at least 90% invested in the home within the statutory deadline.
aidesAudit.interestConfirm: New loan and first subsidy entitlement: ownership, residence, occupancy and income conditions met. For renovation, qualifying works. No subsidy payments already used.
aidesAudit.rightsHint: Land and completed construction subject to duty: confirm with the notary.
aidesAudit.creditConfirm: Private purchase eligible for Bëllegen Akt, occupancy and deadlines met; personal balances and ownership shares checked.
aidesAudit.vatBase: Works eligible for 3% VAT — excluding VAT
aidesAudit.vatRemaining: VAT relief remaining for this dwelling
aidesAudit.vatConfirm: Works and home eligibility checked with AED: use, applicable age or deadlines, net amount and remaining relief confirmed.
aidesAudit.subtotalNote: Excludes unassessed assistance, monthly payments and guarantees. This is not the total of all possible assistance.
aidesAudit.monthly: Initial interest subsidy, outside the total
aidesAudit.scope: Conditional estimate, not an award decision. Bëllegen Akt and VAT relief may already be included in your price or fees: do not deduct them twice. Monthly assistance changes with amortisation and reviews. Special cases and older applications require individual assessment.
aidesAudit.nonRp: Personal purchase grants are not calculated here for rental investment. Landlords may still qualify for energy assistance.
aidesAudit.error: Check amounts, savings years, balances and household composition. No result is retained for invalid data.
aidesAudit.nextNote: For energy work, gather technical advice, areas, performance data, dates and quotes; then obtain eligible amounts and cumulation rules. Announced reforms are not treated as enacted law.

descriptions.bellegen: Based on personal balances, ownership shares and taxable base. Minimum duty €100. Already included in the acquisition-cost calculation.
descriptions.accession: Statutory formula using household composition and 2024/2025 average net income, adjusted for housing type and remaining personal allowances.
descriptions.epargne: 10% of actual annual savings growth, capped at €500/year for ten years per beneficiary. Purchase grant required; shared capital allowance.
descriptions.interet: Indicative initial monthly aid for a new loan: 2025 income, rate rounded down to one eighth of a point, capped capital. Subject to review and statutory amortisation; no 25-year total.
descriptions.garantie: Public guarantee subject to savings, income and bank approval. Neither cash received nor a flat fee saving.
descriptions.tva: 14% of eligible net works, within the remaining €50,000 allowance per dwelling, shared between construction and renovation. Do not deduct from an already reduced price again.
descriptions.klima: Measures, areas, materials, performance, equipment and dates determine the rates. Total cost alone cannot produce a reliable calculation.
descriptions.conseil: Amount depends on the assignment, building and eligible fees; no universal allowance is added automatically.
descriptions.topup: Depends on income, household and eligible state aid, with cumulation limits. No automatic percentage of the works budget.
descriptions.klimapret: Financing and subsidy must be assessed with the bank and housing office. A loan is not a grant and does not guarantee a 1.5% bank rate.
descriptions.privee: Obtain an offer before committing, based on the measure and supplier. No general 5% rate.
descriptions.commune: Rules specific to each municipality and measure, with defined bases and caps. No invented amount for an unknown municipality.

renovationAudit.title: Renovation: scenario budget and returns
renovationAudit.intro: Compare your budget, confirmed grants and expected bill savings. Starting values are editable examples: an energy class alone cannot predict works costs, grants or property appreciation.
renovationAudit.honorairesTTC: Fees and other costs including VAT
renovationAudit.aidesConfirmees: Confirmed grants included in this scenario
renovationAudit.aidNote: Enter documented amounts only; leave 0 if no grant is included. This does not mean you are ineligible. Do not deduct reduced VAT already included in quotes a second time.
renovationAudit.factureApres: Expected annual energy bill after works
renovationAudit.energyNote: Use bills and a consistent technical scenario: comparable usage, occupancy and reference prices before/after. Prices may differ by energy source. Unchanged fixed charges are not savings.
renovationAudit.assumptionsNote: Annual cash flows at year-end. Energy escalation starts in year 2; maintenance stays constant in nominal euros. Grants are paid in the entered year. No automatic resale gain, tax, residual value or unentered future replacement.
renovationAudit.financeNote: Amortising loan with constant monthly payments, excluding insurance and unentered bank fees. The rate is your assumption or offer, not a guaranteed climate-loan rate. Project returns are calculated before financing.
renovationAudit.notDefined: Not defined for these cash flows
renovationAudit.scope: Financial simulation based on your assumptions, without promising grants, an energy class or appreciation. NPV and IRR include entered grants and their timing, but exclude the loan to keep project returns separate from financing. Negative IRRs remain negative; unsupported non-unique-IRR cash flows are shown as undefined.
renovationAudit.interestCost: Interest over the full loan term
renovationAudit.cashAfterDebt: Net savings less debt payments — year 1
renovationAudit.schedule: Annual project cash flows, before financing
renovationAudit.sourceNote: These sources explain eligibility and procedures; they do not validate the costs or savings entered in your scenario.
renovationAudit.error: Check amounts and rates. Grants cannot exceed cost, nor the loan the initial cash requirement. Years must be whole numbers and grant payment within the horizon.

hotelRenovationAudit.intro: Hotel scenario: works budget, documented grants, energy savings and net contribution from additional revenue. Initial ratios are illustrative, not quotes or grant promises.
hotelRenovationAudit.finalEnergy: Billed final energy per heated m²; do not directly use a CPE primary-energy index.
hotelRenovationAudit.autoConso: 0 = illustrative scenario for selected works; replace with technical study. No guaranteed CPE outcome.
hotelRenovationAudit.labelHint: Entered commercial assumption, 0% by default. A label guarantees no RevPAR uplift.
hotelRenovationAudit.quoteHint: Blank = illustrative per-room ratios; enter your quotes. Allocation across items follows ratios, not contractual pricing.
hotelRenovationAudit.margin: Contribution margin on additional revenue after variable costs
hotelRenovationAudit.method: Scenario assumptions, with no validation of cost or technical performance. Entered grants are assumed immediately available and allocated proportionally to costs; no Klimabonus rate is awarded. Commercial gains are multiplied by the entered margin, then added to energy savings net of maintenance. Ten-year NPV at 4%, constant year-end flows, excluding debt, tax, recoverable VAT, future replacements and residual value. Use the detailed scenario for delayed grants or financing.
hotelRenovationAudit.aidTitle: Business grants: check the applicable scheme
hotelRenovationAudit.aidScope: A hotel does not automatically qualify for residential Klimabonus. Verify building use, beneficiary business, eligible expenditure, application date and cumulation rules. Zero included aid means no amount is counted in this scenario, not an ineligibility decision.
hotelRenovationAudit.detailed: Detailed scenario: delayed grants and financing

energyImpactAudit.title: Energy performance: value scenario
energyImpactAudit.description: Test how assumed prices by EPC class affect your property's declared value.
energyImpactAudit.scope: The proposed coefficients are illustrative examples. They are not based on verified transactions and are neither official rates nor a market valuation. No statistical sample or confidence level has been established.
energyImpactAudit.example: Edit each coefficient using your own evidence. D remains at 0%. Proposed values only illustrate the calculation.
energyImpactAudit.invalid: Enter a positive value up to €100 million and coefficients between −90% and +100%.
energyImpactAudit.formula: Target value = current value × (1 + target coefficient / 100) ÷ (1 + current coefficient / 100). The current class retains its declared value exactly.
energyImpactAudit.limits: The calculated difference is not net profit: works, fees and taxes are not deducted. EPC class alone cannot determine actual consumption or CO₂ emissions. Market valuation requires verified comparables and property characteristics.

syndicEnergyAudit.budgetScope: Enter VAT-inclusive quotes and already confirmed grants, all initially zero. No amount is inferred automatically from the EPC class. Results assume grants are immediately available and exclude financing. The target class must be assessed by an energy adviser.
syndicEnergyAudit.invalid: Enter non-negative amounts up to €100 million each. Grants cannot exceed works and fees.
syndicEnergyAudit.valueScope: Market value cannot be inferred from a fixed national price or EPC class alone. Use verified comparables and a separate sensitivity scenario.
syndicEnergyAudit.epbd: For residential buildings, the EPBD sets a national average-consumption trajectory. An EPC letter alone does not establish an individual 2030 or 2033 deadline. Applicable national rules must be checked for the building.
syndicEnergyAudit.allocation: Allocation by ownership shares is a budgeting assumption. Each beneficiary's eligibility and the building's allocation rules must be checked; grants are not automatically transferable between units.

energySharingAudit.title: Electricity sharing: financial balance
energySharingAudit.intro: Compare annual cash flows for consumers, the producer and the combined group.
energySharingAudit.scope: Proposed values are editable examples, with no guaranteed tariff or grant. The producer bears the investment and annual costs; consumers pay for shared electricity and residual charges. The collective balance combines both.
energySharingAudit.timing: Shared energy must come from measurements or a study of simultaneous generation and consumption profiles. An annual balance alone does not demonstrate feasibility.
energySharingAudit.productionNote: Enter generation from a study or measurements. PVGIS provides a climate-based estimate, not measured generation or proof of shareable volume.
energySharingAudit.invalid: Check inputs: shared energy cannot exceed generation or consumption; grants cannot exceed investment. Whole consumer count from 1 to 10,000; tariffs from 0 to 10 €/kWh (exports: −10 to +10); other amounts from 0 to 1 billion.
energySharingAudit.notRecovered: Not recovered with this constant cash flow
energySharingAudit.allocation: The consumer average is not a contractual allocation rule. Collective payback is relevant only if the group bears the investment and receives all the cash flows.
energySharingAudit.formula: Consumers = shared kWh × (avoided price − sharing price − residual charges). Producer = sharing payments + surplus sales − annual costs. Collective = consumers + producer: the internal sharing price cancels out.
energySharingAudit.limits: Constant cash flows, immediate grant, no borrowing, discounting, panel degradation or additional tax calculation. Use contractual prices; fixed charges that are not avoided are excluded. Losses, batteries and hourly profiles belong in the generation study. These figures establish neither legal compliance nor CO₂ savings.

epbdAudit.title: EPBD: European building targets
epbdAudit.intro: Distinguish building-stock targets from the rules to check for your own building.
epbdAudit.scope: These notes summarise the European directive. An EPC letter alone cannot determine a non-compliance date, renovation duty or rental prohibition. This page does not certify building compliance.
epbdAudit.residentialText: The directive provides for a reduction in average primary energy use across the national residential stock of at least 16% by 2030 and 20–22% by 2035, compared with 2020. This is not a class E requirement in 2030 or class D in 2033 for every home. National measures and exemptions must be examined.
epbdAudit.nonResidentialText: Countries must set maximum energy-performance thresholds corresponding to the worst-performing 16% and then 26% of their national non-residential reference stock in 2020. European deadlines are 2030 and 2033. These percentages do not mean identical reductions for each building and do not automatically translate into Luxembourg EPC letters.
epbdAudit.newText: The European zero-emission building objective applies to new buildings owned by public bodies from 1 January 2028, then to all new buildings from 1 January 2030, subject to the relevant provisions and exemptions. National requirements and the project's circumstances must be checked.
epbdAudit.nationalText: Consult current Luxembourg legislation, building use, project characteristics, applicable thresholds and exemptions. The amended Grand Ducal Regulation of 9 June 2021 and ministry technical resources are starting points. The general transposition deadline of 29 May 2026 does not itself prove that a specific duty applies to your building. The long-term European objective is a zero-emission building stock by 2050.
epbdAudit.valueText: The directive establishes no automatic price discount. Value changes depend on the market, works and property characteristics and require a separate valuation.
epbdAudit.source2: Ministry of the Economy — technical information

cpePreparationAudit.title: Prepare your home's EPC assessment
cpePreparationAudit.intro: Gather useful property characteristics and documents before contacting an authorised expert.
cpePreparationAudit.scope: A general questionnaire cannot calculate an EPC. Energy performance, thermal insulation and emissions are separate indicators. No score, EPC letter, theoretical cost or emissions are assigned here.
cpePreparationAudit.summary: Summary to review with the expert
cpePreparationAudit.expert: This is self-reported information. An EPC requires detailed technical data and an authorised professional; the procedure for an existing home includes a visit.
cpePreparationAudit.measurements: Ratio from your meter or bill records
cpePreparationAudit.measurementNote: Enter delivered energy in kWh over 12 months and the area covering the same scope. The quotient adjusts for neither climate nor occupancy; it does not convert final to primary energy or determine an EPC class. The entered area is not automatically the official energy reference area.
cpePreparationAudit.missing: Enter non-negative energy and a strictly positive area to calculate the ratio.
cpePreparationAudit.documentsText: Prepare available plans, wall and insulation details, installation specifications and any existing EPC. For an existing building, Guichet.lu mentions thermal-energy bills or readings for the previous three years. The exact list depends on the project.

energyPortfolioAudit.intro: Inventory of declared EPC classes, floor areas and entered values. Import your properties or add them manually.
energyPortfolioAudit.scope: Copy the energy performance class from a valid EPC, not its insulation class or environmental indicator. “?” means unknown. Data stays in this browser; export a CSV to keep a backup.
energyPortfolioAudit.method: Values are the amounts you enter, with no automatic premium or discount. An EPC letter alone cannot determine actual consumption, CO₂ emissions or renovation costs. These require records and a study suited to the building.
energyPortfolioAudit.regulation: The class alone does not establish a renovation obligation by 2030 or 2033. The EPBD distinguishes a national residential trajectory from national thresholds for non-residential buildings. Check the Luxembourg rules applicable to each building; this inventory does not certify compliance or Taxonomy or CRREM alignment.
energyPortfolioAudit.impactLink: Build a value scenario using your assumptions
energyPortfolioAudit.storageError: The saved portfolio cannot be read or contains invalid data. It has been preserved unchanged. Download the original to recover it before correcting the saved data.
energyPortfolioAudit.saveError: Saving in this browser failed. Export your portfolio as CSV to retain your changes.
energyPortfolioAudit.empty: Add a property with its declared EPC class, floor area and value.
energyPortfolioAudit.distributionNote: Distribution of entered areas, including those with no known class. Letters are not averaged: this chart is not a collective EPC. Residential and non-residential methods differ; this distribution is a descriptive inventory only.

mortgageConditionsAudit.title: Compare financing conditions
mortgageConditionsAudit.intro: Compare two assumptions or bank proposals for the same principal and term. No rate or ceiling is automatically derived from the EPC.
mortgageConditionsAudit.example: Initial values are an example, not market offers. Enter your own conditions.
mortgageConditionsAudit.invalid: Enter valid values: positive principal and value, whole term from 1 to 50 years, rates from 0 to 30%, ratios from 0 to 100%.
mortgageConditionsAudit.monthly: Monthly payment excluding fees and insurance
mortgageConditionsAudit.gapNote: The requested principal exceeds this ceiling: the payment still uses your request and is not an available loan offer.
mortgageConditionsAudit.limits: Fully amortising loan at a fixed rate throughout, monthly payments at period end, no deferral. Interest = payment × number of months − principal. Fees, insurance, taxes, subsidies and early repayments are excluded; no APR is calculated.
mortgageConditionsAudit.ltvNote: The ceiling is only value × entered ratio. It is not borrowing capacity: income, expenses, collateral, lender valuation and CSSF rules must still be assessed. An entered limit is neither a right to credit nor regulatory approval.
mortgageConditionsAudit.cpeNote: Any energy-related preferential conditions depend on the offer and application. An EPC class alone does not guarantee a green loan, a rate, EPBD compliance or absence of climate risk.
mortgageConditionsAudit.source: CSSF — Regulation 20-08 on residential property credit

loanOffersAudit.title: Compare three loan proposals
loanOffersAudit.intro: Enter your proposals for the same principal. The calculation separates interest, insurance, fees and principal repaid.
loanOffersAudit.example: The three identical scenarios are examples, not bank offers. Complete the zero costs; zero does not mean no charge will apply.
loanOffersAudit.invalid: Complete all inputs: positive principal, whole term from 1 to 50 years, rate from 0 to 30%, non-negative costs.
loanOffersAudit.rankingNote: For identical principal and term, the lowest entered cost is marked, including ties. This does not compare coverage or contractual flexibility.
loanOffersAudit.differentTerms: Terms differ: amounts are shown without selecting a best proposal. A lower payment does not mean a cheaper loan.
loanOffersAudit.formula: Fully amortising fixed-rate loan for the entire term, payments at month end. Cost excluding principal = interest + insurance + other fees. Upfront costs are paid in cash initially; monthly costs run for the whole term.
loanOffersAudit.insuranceNote: Copy the insurance quote: upfront and/or monthly premiums as contracted, without counting a premium twice. This model does not calculate insurance that varies with the outstanding balance; confirm requirements and coverage with the lender and insurer.
loanOffersAudit.limits: No regulatory APR is calculated. Unknown costs, taxes, subsidies, rate changes, deferrals and early repayments are not modelled. Financed premiums or fees require a separate financing plan to avoid double counting.
loanOffersAudit.ratesNote: Use the nominal rate in your proposal. BCL statistics are averages, not individual offers or guaranteed rates. A rate fixed only for an initial period must not be applied to the full term without an explicit assumption.

loanPlanningAudit.fees: Compensation and fees quoted by lender (EUR)
loanPlanningAudit.strategy: Method to agree with the lender
loanPlanningAudit.invalid: Enter non-negative amounts, a whole term of 1–50 years, rate of 0–30%, ratio of 0–100% and a month within the term. Original principal must be positive.
loanPlanningAudit.source: CSSF — Mortgage credit and early repayment
loanPlanningAudit.result_loanBudget: Budget available for principal and interest
loanPlanningAudit.result_recoveryMonths: Time for avoided interest to cover fees
loanPlanningAudit.capacityIntro: The 40% ratio is an editable assumption, not a universal legal ceiling. Complete the new loan costs, initially zero.
loanPlanningAudit.capacityMethod: Loan budget = income × ratio − existing commitments − insurance − other monthly fees, floored at zero. Principal is derived from this budget for constant monthly payments at a fixed rate throughout.
loanPlanningAudit.capacityLimits: Existing commitments and the ratio must cover the same items. This does not assess all living expenses, disposable income, collateral, LTV or lender approval. Single premiums, upfront or variable costs need a separate financing plan. This principal is not an all-in purchase budget.
loanPlanningAudit.prepaymentIntro: The operation takes place immediately after the selected instalment. Enter compensation and fees from the lender statement: zero is an assumption to confirm, not an exemption.
loanPlanningAudit.prepaymentMethod: The rate stays fixed, with monthly payments at period end. Repayment is limited to the remaining principal; any excess request is displayed. Entered fees apply only if principal is actually repaid. The final instalment may be smaller than the usual payment.
loanPlanningAudit.prepaymentLimits: Reconcile the balance with the lender statement. The displayed saving only covers avoided interest less entered fees, excluding insurance, tax, discounting and alternative savings returns. The displayed recovery time covers fees through avoided interest, not the capital used. It is not a repayment recommendation.
loanPlanningAudit.legal: The six-month interest cap depends notably on the property having been the actual main home for at least two uninterrupted years; it does not cover the portion of cumulative early repayments exceeding EUR 450,000. This simulator does not calculate the statutory compensation: check the contract and statement with the lender.

bankingBasicsAudit.ltvIntro: Simple ratio of the entered loan to the property value. Enter the value used by your bank.
bankingBasicsAudit.difference: Value not covered by the loan (€), excluding fees
bankingBasicsAudit.ltvNote: This ratio determines neither credit approval nor the total cash contribution required. Acquisition costs are excluded. CSSF Regulation 20-08 distinguishes borrower categories and provides conditions and flexibility: your bank must assess your application and the regulatory calculation basis.
bankingBasicsAudit.dscrIntro: Use the same 12-month period for all amounts. Rent must reflect vacancy and unpaid rent; operating costs exclude loan principal, interest and personal income tax.
bankingBasicsAudit.debt: Principal and interest due in the year (€)
bankingBasicsAudit.dscrNote: DSCR = net operating income / debt service. At 1, income exactly covers debt; below 1, it does not. A ratio above 1 does not guarantee financing: each lender sets its conditions. With no debt service, the ratio is undefined.
bankingBasicsAudit.amortizationIntro: Fully amortizing loan with a constant nominal rate, payments at month end and full disbursement at inception. Insurance, fees, grace periods and rate changes excluded. Contractual bank rounding may cause small differences.
bankingBasicsAudit.monthly: Monthly payment excluding fees and insurance (€)
bankingBasicsAudit.invalid: Complete all fields with valid values. Property value and principal must be positive; amounts from 0 to €1 trillion, rates from 0 to 30%, whole terms from 1 to 50 years. DSCR requires positive debt service.
bankingBasicsAudit.example: Initial values are editable examples, not credit offers.

agencyPresentationAudit.scope: Commercial brochure based on your information. Initial numbers are examples to replace; no independent valuation is calculated here.
agencyPresentationAudit.valuationNote: The range applies your percentage to your central value. It is neither a confidence interval nor a Tevaxia appraisal.
agencyPresentationAudit.includeValuation: Include the entered value and range
agencyPresentationAudit.feesScope: Existing dwelling, ordinary sale: 6% registration + 1% transcription, before Bëllegen Akt and without special reductions. Statutory sale emolument including 17% VAT. Mortgage, disbursements, copies, bank fees and agency fees excluded: this subtotal is not the full budget.
agencyPresentationAudit.feesUnsupported: For this property type or an off-plan sale, obtain a notarial quote for your file. No automatic subtotal is added to the PDF.
agencyPresentationAudit.existing: Existing dwelling, not an off-plan sale
agencyPresentationAudit.energyNote: Copy both classes from the valid energy certificate. This brochure neither calculates nor certifies it. For land, leave the classes unspecified.
agencyPresentationAudit.invalid: Check the information: positive price and area, finite numbers, bedrooms ≤ rooms, whole years and room counts, range from 0 to 100%.
agencyPresentationAudit.error: Generation failed. Please retry; your entries are preserved.
agencyPresentationAudit.financeNote: Simulation at a constant nominal rate, payments at month end, excluding insurance and bank fees. The deposit applies to the price; quantified fees are additional. This is not a credit offer.

energyQuestionnaireAudit.title: Prepare an energy assessment
energyQuestionnaireAudit.intro: 20 questions to gather information before meeting a professional. You may answer “I do not know”. This questionnaire does not calculate your building’s energy performance.
energyQuestionnaireAudit.scope: These answers cannot establish an energy certificate class, an energy score, savings or grant amounts. Budget, occupancy and renovation plans are not measures of building performance.
energyQuestionnaireAudit.documents: Documents and points to discuss with the professional
energyQuestionnaireAudit.envelope: Envelope: plans, areas, insulation composition and thickness, renovation invoices, window specifications and observed defects.
energyQuestionnaireAudit.heating: Heating: system reference and power, maintenance, emitters, controls and energy bills from the last three years. Selecting a replacement requires a tailored study.
energyQuestionnaireAudit.ventilation: Ventilation: existing system, maintenance, air renewal and signs of damp. Have the causes assessed before defining works.
energyQuestionnaireAudit.water: Hot water: equipment, capacity, age, maintenance and usage. Separate its consumption from heating where readings allow.
energyQuestionnaireAudit.usage: Use and project: reference area, occupancy, comfort goals, constraints and budget. Study works together; their savings cannot simply be added.
energyQuestionnaireAudit.grants: Grants depend on works, technical criteria, dates and application steps. Check current conditions and obtain confirmation; no flat percentage is applied here.
energyQuestionnaireAudit.source: Guichet.lu — energy certificate and useful documents
energyQuestionnaireAudit.progress: Questionnaire progress, not an energy score

hvacScenarioAudit.title: Heating: compare needs, quotations and costs
hvacScenarioAudit.intro: Compare two scenarios using entered heat needs, seasonal performance, prices and quotations. Initial values illustrate the method; they are neither measurements of your property nor commercial offers.
hvacScenarioAudit.quotes: Quotations by work package, including VAT
hvacScenarioAudit.quoteNote: Enter quotation totals including the applicable VAT. Zero means no cost is counted for that package: check for omissions. The eight lines must not overlap.
hvacScenarioAudit.payback: Simple payback within the entered horizon
hvacScenarioAudit.balance: Nominal balance at the entered horizon
hvacScenarioAudit.missingBudget: No priced quotation: the budget is incomplete and payback is not calculated.
hvacScenarioAudit.energyNote: Purchased energy = useful heat / seasonal factor. For boilers, use seasonal efficiency consistent with the fuel; for heat pumps, seasonal performance suited to climate and temperatures, not a single-point COP. Use the same heating/hot-water scope and avoid counting auxiliaries twice in other costs.
hvacScenarioAudit.powerNote: Outputs come from the study and technical sheet at the same outdoor and water-flow temperatures. Their arithmetic difference does not certify EN 12831 sizing, modulation, backup, defrost, hot water or emitter suitability. No unit or ventilation flow is automatically selected.
hvacScenarioAudit.financialNote: Saving = cost before − cost after; higher running costs stay negative. Simple payback = net cost / positive annual saving, only when reached within the horizon. Nominal balance = annual savings × horizon − net cost. Constant prices, excluding discounting, finance, taxes, replacements, degradation and resale.
hvacScenarioAudit.aidNote: Only enter grants confirmed for the application; otherwise leave zero. Reduced VAT already included in the quotation must not be deducted twice. The calculator does not determine Klimabonus, enoprimes or VAT eligibility.
hvacScenarioAudit.invalid: Check fields: finite nonnegative amounts, seasonal factors greater than zero and at most 10, whole horizon from 1 to 50 years, grants no greater than quotations.

lenozThresholdAudit.title: LENOZ: check classification thresholds
lenozThresholdAudit.intro: Enter achievement percentages from your complete LENOZ file to check the ministry’s published thresholds. This page does not replace the expert’s assessment of the criteria.
lenozThresholdAudit.scope: The overall percentage must come from the file’s LENOZ calculation; it is not the simple average of the percentages below. Only thresholds are checked, without verifying evidence, applicable criteria, weightings or grants.
lenozThresholdAudit.result: Thresholds met by the entered values
lenozThresholdAudit.level0: No class: 40% overall threshold not reached
lenozThresholdAudit.resultNote: This result is neither a certificate nor the award of a label. The data and complete file must be validated by a competent professional.
lenozThresholdAudit.exceptions: Category minima apply to economy, ecology, building and technical installations, and functionality. They do not apply to location and society. Class 4 has no category minimum.
lenozThresholdAudit.invalid: Complete all five percentages with numbers from 0 to 100. No result or PDF is produced when any value is missing or invalid.
lenozThresholdAudit.source2: Housing Ministry — sample file and evidence

taxonomyAudit.title: EU Taxonomy: prepare a 7.7 review
taxonomyAudit.intro: Acquisition and ownership of buildings, climate change mitigation. Check thresholds and gather supporting documents for a file review.
taxonomyAudit.scope: This preliminary check relies on your declarations. It does not certify documents, Taxonomy alignment or green financing. Construction activity 7.1, renovation 7.2 and the adaptation objective require separate analysis. A professional must confirm the criteria applicable at acquisition and the exact property scope.
taxonomyAudit.period: Time regime established in the file
taxonomyAudit.periodNote: Confirm the relevant date using permit documents and the Commission FAQ, including the construction permit application date. Do not infer the regime solely from the property's marketed construction year.
taxonomyAudit.route: Evidence pathway for an older building
taxonomyAudit.thresholdNote: Older: a national or regional stock study covering buildings built before 31 December 2020, distinguishing at least residential and non-residential. Newer: the national nZEB threshold applicable to the property, compared at 90%. No assumed Luxembourg threshold is supplied; use the same indicator and scope.
taxonomyAudit.area: Building area relevant to the 5,000 m² threshold
taxonomyAudit.power: Effective rated output of the relevant system (kW)
taxonomyAudit.powerNote: Heating, combined heating and ventilation, air conditioning or combined air conditioning and ventilation: monitoring applies to non-residential buildings above 290 kW. Have the expert confirm the system scope; unknown output is not zero.
taxonomyAudit.answerNote: “Yes” means the point is declared satisfied with supporting evidence in the file. This page does not receive or verify the documents.
taxonomyAudit.epcEvidence: Valid EPC and PED evidence matching the scope (as-built EPC for newer buildings)
taxonomyAudit.thresholdEvidence: Applicable top-15% study or nZEB threshold with source, date and method documented
taxonomyAudit.envelope: Above 5,000 m²: air-tightness and thermal integrity checks, with disclosure of deviations
taxonomyAudit.largeNote: For newer buildings, Section 7.1 requires air-tightness and thermal integrity testing and disclosure of deviations and defects to investors/clients. Robust, traceable quality control during construction can replace thermal integrity testing. Life-cycle GWP must be calculated for each stage and disclosed on request. Confirm the building area and evidence even when acquiring an individual unit.
taxonomyAudit.gwp: Above 5,000 m²: life-cycle GWP calculated and available to investors and clients
taxonomyAudit.monitoring: Efficient operation evidenced by energy performance monitoring and assessment
taxonomyAudit.adaptation: Documented review against Appendix A: climate risks, vulnerability and necessary solutions
taxonomyAudit.adaptationNote: The review must cover relevant physical risks over the lifetime, suitable scenarios and measures required under Appendix A. A finding of no risk or no necessary measure needs evidence. For activity 7.7 DNSH, water, circularity, pollution and biodiversity are marked not applicable; other legal obligations still apply.
taxonomyAudit.safeguards: Undertaking's procedures reviewed against Article 18 minimum safeguards
taxonomyAudit.safeguardsNote: Minimum safeguards include OECD guidelines, UN guiding principles, fundamental labour rights and human rights. A policy statement alone does not replace procedures and review; this assessment belongs to the file of the undertaking carrying out the activity.
taxonomyAudit.energy: Energy criterion of the selected pathway
taxonomyAudit.issues: Some declared points do not meet the criteria
taxonomyAudit.review: Declared points are ready for professional review
taxonomyAudit.source0: Regulation 2021/2139, Annex I, Sections 7.1 and 7.7, Appendix A — consolidated 1 January 2026
taxonomyAudit.source2: Regulation 2020/852, Articles 3 and 18: conditions and minimum safeguards

trajectoryAudit.title: Compare energy and carbon trajectories
trajectoryAudit.intro: Calculate intensities from a documented annual report, then compare a building scenario year by year with a reference trajectory you provide.
trajectoryAudit.scope: This arithmetic comparison is not a certified CRREM assessment, an EPC, Taxonomy compliance or an estimate of value loss. No CRREM curve, emission factor or automatic renovation scenario is embedded.
trajectoryAudit.metricsNote: Use the same period, area and building coverage for both reports. Check tenant and common-area uses, vacancy, on-site renewables and refrigerant emissions. Heat-pump electricity consumption must not be divided by COP a second time. Dividing by area does not perform CRREM normalisations.
trajectoryAudit.referenceNote: Identify source, version, country, property type, starting year, carbon scope and projection assumptions. Building columns must reflect documented changes in consumption and emission factors. The report intensities above are not automatically extended into the future.
trajectoryAudit.inputNote: Five columns in this order: year; target energy; target carbon; building energy; building carbon. Semicolon or tab separator, decimal comma or dot, no thousands separators. Energy in kWh/m²/year and carbon in kg CO₂e/m²/year. At least two consecutive years from 2000 to 2150; no gaps, duplicates or blank cells. No interpolation or extrapolation.
trajectoryAudit.invalid: Enter valid values and a file reference to display the comparison.
trajectoryAudit.source0: CRREM: library, assessment guide and official data
trajectoryAudit.source1: European Commission: Energy Performance of Buildings Directive
trajectoryAudit.officialNote: For a CRREM assessment, use official data matching the property and the full methodology, including normalisations and emission-factor projections. Commercial integration is subject to CRREM licensing terms. An exceedance year does not establish a rental ban or value loss; no “net zero” result is inferred from the target curve.
trajectoryAudit.exampleReference: Fictional educational example — no official trajectory
trajectoryAudit.exampleNote: Fictional example: equality in 2026, exceedance of 10 kWh/m² and 1 kg CO₂e/m² in 2027, back below targets in 2028. It illustrates arithmetic and does not represent a building or CRREM trajectory.

esgDossierAudit.title: Property environment and valuation assumptions
esgDossierAudit.intro: Record known information from the file. Equipment or an energy class does not automatically create a premium or discount.
esgDossierAudit.scope: This environmental record is not a complete ESG rating, technical audit or RICS/TEGOVA certification. It does not alone cover social and governance matters. Declarations, documents, costs, rents, risks and comparables require assessment in the property's context.
esgDossierAudit.epc: Primary-energy class of the valid EPC
esgDossierAudit.certifications: Declared certifications: name, version, scope and validity
esgDossierAudit.references: Sources and dates of file checks
esgDossierAudit.referenceNote: Identify maps, studies, attestations and inspections used. A “no” answer needs evidence; it does not establish the absence of all risk. A certificate, equipment and its performance are different things.
esgDossierAudit.countNote: These counts show progress through seven answers only, without a quality score or risk weighting. EPC, certification and reference fields remain information to review.
esgDossierAudit.sensitivityNote: The percentage is your assumption, not an observed rate calculated by Tevaxia. Explain comparable selection and adjustments. Avoid counting an effect already included in rents, yield, works or the reference value twice. Zero means no effect is quantified here, not that no effect exists.
esgDossierAudit.invalid: Enter a positive value and a valid percentage; any non-zero assumption needs a rationale.
esgDossierAudit.resultNote: This sensitivity remains separate from other valuation methods and is not automatically included in their result or the valuation PDF.
esgDossierAudit.source: RICS: ESG factors in commercial property valuation, 2026 edition

renovationResidualAudit.title: Residual value: a documented renovation scenario
renovationResidualAudit.intro: Subtract a renovation budget from an assumed post-works value, using the same valuation date and scope. Costs come from the file, not an EPC class jump.
renovationResidualAudit.reference: References for quotations, grants, post-works value and valuation date
renovationResidualAudit.scope: This formula is a cost sensitivity: it does not establish a market discount, sale price or EVS/CRR compliance. It does not calculate a future EPC or necessary works. A professional must review comparables, timing, discounting, tax and any other costs.
renovationResidualAudit.costNote: Use VAT-inclusive amounts under the file's actual VAT regime. The selected contingency applies to works + fees + financing costs. Zero means no amount included: check omissions. Avoid duplicate costs across quotations, fees and financing.
renovationResidualAudit.grantNote: Use zero without a confirmed grant. Do not deduct VAT savings already reflected in quotations. Grants cannot exceed the budget including contingency. This calculation does not assess eligibility or payment dates.
renovationResidualAudit.invalid: Enter valid value and costs, a file reference and a contingency from 0 to 100%. Grants must be between zero and the total budget.
renovationResidualAudit.negative: The balance is negative: net costs exceed the entered post-works value. This is not converted into a zero market value.
renovationResidualAudit.resultNote: No result is automatically transferred to other methods or the valuation PDF. This subtraction does not replace an analysis using dated cash flows.
renovationResidualAudit.linkNote: An energy-class jump is insufficient to price works. Use a building study and detailed quotations; no cost envelope is automatically inferred from this estimate.
renovationResidualAudit.link: Compare a renovation project using documented inputs

termReversionAudit.title: Term and reversion — annual scenario
termReversionAudit.intro: Initial values are an example. Enter annual rents net of non-recoverable costs and yields supported by your file, with a consistent scope.
termReversionAudit.scope: Convention: annual rents in arrears, constant passing rent during the term, then constant ERV in perpetuity from the following year. ERV is not automatically grown. Acquisition costs, tax, works, vacancy and other cash flows are not calculated here. Yields and rents require comparable analysis; no risk level is inferred automatically.
termReversionAudit.initial: Simple initial yield: passing rent / value
termReversionAudit.explanation: Equivalent yield is the common rate applied to term and reversion that reproduces the same value. It is solved numerically, not calculated as ERV / value. Displayed simple yields exclude acquisition costs.
termReversionAudit.invalid: Valid rents, positive ERV and reversion yield, and a whole term from 0 to 100 years are required. Invalid results do not feed reconciliation.
termReversionAudit.undefined: Not calculable with zero passing rent
termReversionAudit.same: Passing rent equals the entered ERV
termReversionAudit.reference: Notes and references for rents and yields
termReversionAudit.transfer: This method feeds the income-approach value used in reconciliation. It does not by itself constitute a certified market valuation.
termReversionAudit.source: RICS: investment method, term/reversion and equivalent yield

prudentialAudit.title: Value sensitivity and prudential file
prudentialAudit.scope: Test documented reductions to the reference value. This arithmetic calculation determines neither a Mortgage Lending Value (MLV) nor a CRR-compliant property value.
prudentialAudit.regulation: Prudential valuation requires, among other things, an independent appraisal, conservative criteria, transparent documentation and compliance with applicable caps. The banking file must address the legal regime, original value, revaluations and relevant risks.
prudentialAudit.baseNote: Value from reconciliation of valuation methods; displaying it does not certify market value. Complete the valuation methods first.
prudentialAudit.reference: Dated valuation reference, justification of reductions and supporting documents
prudentialAudit.formula: Percentages are added and applied once to the reference value; their sum must not exceed 100%. Avoid counting adjustments already included in the methods twice.
prudentialAudit.noTransfer: This scenario does not replace reconciliation and is not automatically transferred to the report.
prudentialAudit.invalid: Provide a file reference and a positive value from the valuation methods. Reductions must be finite, non-negative and total at most 100%.
prudentialAudit.weights: No risk weight or lending limit is inferred here. These depend on the exposure type, property, collateral, prudential regime and the conditions in CRR Articles 124–126, among other factors.

bankApiAudit.title: Property estimation API for banks
bankApiAudit.intro: Integrate an indicative Luxembourg apartment estimate into your workflow. Review the data, assumptions and limits before using results in a credit decision.
bankApiAudit.scope: The /api/v1/estimation API uses the public estimator's calculation: a municipal reference and internal adjustments. It supports freehold apartments, existing or off-plan when segment data is available.
bankApiAudit.data: The currently integrated references come from the Housing Observatory publications of 25 June 2026. Unavailable prices are not replaced with fictional individual sales.
bankApiAudit.limits: The range is conventional, with no measured statistical accuracy. The result is neither a signed appraisal, a TEGOVA-certified market value nor a financing decision.
bankApiAudit.auth: Use a server API key in Authorization: Bearer or X-API-Key. Do not expose it in public browser code. The example below uses the actual accepted field names.
bankApiAudit.response: A successful response contains success, data and meta. data includes estimationCentrale, estimationBasse, estimationHaute, prixM2Base, prixM2Ajuste, sourceBase and ajustements. meta describes the method and limits; no comparable-sale count, recommended LTV or certified MLV is returned.
bankApiAudit.errors: Handle errors: 400 for invalid requests, 401 for authentication, 404 when no estimate is available, 429 for call limits and 500 for server errors.
bankApiAudit.prudential: The legacy /api/v1/mlv path calculates arithmetic sensitivity to entered reductions. Its mlv and ratioMLVsurMV fields describe this scenario only; ltvBands is empty and the result is marked non-regulatory. It does not validate CRR requirements or risk weights.
bankApiAudit.integration: Check your use cases, required data, error handling and human review. An address alone does not provide all the characteristics needed for an estimate.
bankApiAudit.logging: Logging for database-managed keys records the key identifier, endpoint, status, call duration and last use. This description is not a general privacy guarantee: processing scope, retention and service providers must be documented contractually.
bankApiAudit.availability: Agree availability, response times, hosting, quotas and service commitments before integration. No numerical performance or guaranteed update frequency is stated here.

reconciliationAudit.title: Method reconciliation
reconciliationAudit.scope: Review values for the same property, date and scope. The weighted average helps compare assumptions; it does not certify market value.
reconciliationAudit.weights: Initial weights are illustrative. Only available methods with a positive weight are retained; their weights are normalised to 100%. A missing method does not mechanically reduce the value.
reconciliationAudit.note: Working note: reasons for selecting methods and weights
reconciliationAudit.noteScope: This note stays in this tab and is not exported. Add the justification and evidence to the final file.
reconciliationAudit.transfer: This value and the retained weights are used for saving, PDF/DOCX exports, sharing and the prudential section. No fallback value is invented when methods are absent or excluded.
reconciliationAudit.dispersionNote: These differences describe the retained methods, not statistical accuracy, a confidence interval or an EVS compliance threshold. Convergence can result from shared assumptions.
reconciliationAudit.invalid: No value to retain: check available values and weights (numbers from 0 to 100). At least one positive method value must have a positive weight.
reconciliationAudit.scenarioNote: These chosen variations apply to the weighted value. They do not recalculate rents, vacancy or method rates, do not form a statistical range and are not automatically exported.
reconciliationAudit.scenarioInvalid: A retained value and two percentages from 0 to 100 are required.

comparisonAudit.title: Comparison of documented sales
comparisonAudit.scope: This calculation uses the sales you enter. Verify the transaction, rights sold, ancillary areas, terms and an area definition consistent with the subject property. This tool has no individual sales database.
comparisonAudit.marketNote: The municipal average describes a group of transactions. It is neither an individual comparable sale nor a house, land or commercial property value. It does not populate calculation prices or adjustments.
comparisonAudit.formula: Adjusted unit price = sale price ÷ area × (1 + sum of adjustments ÷ 100). The weighted average is multiplied by the subject area. Weights are relative; zero excludes a reference.
comparisonAudit.adjustmentNote: Adjustments are additive. A positive adjustment raises the reference price to make it comparable to the subject. No statistical schedule, date index or automatic coefficient is applied.
comparisonAudit.justification: Reasons for adjustments and relevance (including no adjustment)
comparisonAudit.resultNote: The result depends on the author’s selection and checks. The number of references and their weights do not measure accuracy. Include the evidence and reasoning in the final file.
comparisonAudit.invalid: Complete each reference: address, source, valid non-future sale month, positive price and area, reasons and weight from 0 to 100. At least one weight must be positive. Each adjustment must be from −100 to 100%, and their sum greater than −100%.
comparisonAudit.methodSource: RICS — use and verification of comparable evidence

valuationSession.persistence: Inputs are retained between tabs and modes during this page session. Reset clears all forms. Closing or reloading may lose these inputs.
valuationSession.incomeSource: Selected income method (last income tab viewed)

valuationScope.title: Property valuation — scenarios and evidence
valuationScope.intro: Compare documented sales, capitalise income or discount cash flows, then choose weights suited to your file.
valuationScope.basis: These calculations do not automatically determine market rent, liquidation value or a CRR prudential value. A professional basis of value requires documented scope, assumptions and analysis.
valuationScope.asset: The asset type identifies the file. It does not automatically change income, rates or adjustments. Check their relevance to the property and valuation date.
valuationScope.inputs: Initial method inputs are examples to replace. No market rate, regulatory haircut or compliance score is inferred from the asset type.
valuationScope.surfaceInvalid: Enter a positive finite area of at most 10,000,000 m² to obtain a reconciliation or export.
valuationScope.review: The author must document method selection, evidence, property checks and conclusions. Completing the form does not certify EVS, TEGOVA or CRR compliance.

reportDraftAudit.title: Valuation file draft
reportDraftAudit.scope: Calculator PDF and DOCX files summarize calculations. To retain the text and choices in this draft, use its HTML export: all sections, including collapsed ones, are included. Open the file in a browser to read or print it.
reportDraftAudit.review: Uncertified draft. The author must verify statements, qualifications, dates, evidence and conclusions. An unchecked box is not a negative finding. References to standards do not prove compliance.
reportDraftAudit.independence: Disclose relationships, interests and potential conflicts after checking. The software does not presume independence.
reportDraftAudit.competence: Enter your exact qualifications and validity in the author section; the software does not verify them.
reportDraftAudit.esg: Document relevant environmental factors and their property-specific effects. No alignment, premium or regulatory risk is certified here.
reportDraftAudit.annexes: List of documents you must attach to the final file. Checking a box does not add files or appendices to calculation PDFs.
reportDraftAudit.evidence: References validated in the calculator. Adjustments in order: location, condition, floor, exterior, parking, date, other. The author must attach supporting evidence.

dcfLeaseAudit.title: Multi-tenant DCF — expected monthly cash flows
dcfLeaseAudit.scope: Deterministic scenario: identical inputs give identical results. Initial parameters are indicative and examples fictional. Monthly flows are grouped by year and discounted at year-end.
dcfLeaseAudit.rentScope: Enter current annual rent at the valuation date, or initial rent for a future lease. Annual indexation starts from that reference date. Past rent steps are assumed already included in current rent. Start and end months are included; rent-free months apply at the actual lease start.
dcfLeaseAudit.renewalScope: A supplied early exit date is assumed exercised at month-end. After that exit or lease expiry, expected rent equals ERV × occupancy probability × (1 − ERV vacancy). ERV is constant. There are no random draws or simulated reletting schedules.
dcfLeaseAudit.chargesScope: Tenant reimbursements are matched by equal expenses and create no profit. Fixed non-recoverable costs include costs retained during vacancy. Fit-out contribution is paid once at the actual lease start. The recurring annual CAPEX reserve is deducted from cash flows and the terminal base.
dcfLeaseAudit.terminalScope: Terminal value capitalises forecast recurring year N+1 cash flow and then holds it constant forever. Selling costs and the known N+1 fit-out contribution, discounted one year, are deducted. Later changes are not projected: choose a horizon covering key expiries and test exit assumptions.
dcfLeaseAudit.investmentScope: This valuation is not an investment return calculation. Acquisition price, financing and tax are not modelled; no IRR is inferred from the calculated price.
dcfLeaseAudit.currentRent: Current annual rent / initial for a future lease
dcfLeaseAudit.steps: Future rent steps: lease year;annual rent — one per line (e.g. 2;24000)
